text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyGiant, Fruit-Eating Bats Are ShrinkingLeaving Madagascar with smaller pollinatorsDRBy Devin Reese9:00 AM CST on November 14, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleOn Madagascar, a furry creature with a puppy-like nose is a key player in pollination. The bat, called the Madagascan flying fox (Pteropus rufus), gulps down fruits, flowers, and nectar, resulting in dustings of pollen all over its face. With a wingspan of up to 5 feet, these bats travel as far as 30 miles during their foraging journeys, unwittingly spreading pollen far and wide. Powered By 00:00/13:39108.9K 00ShareNextStayBut a new study published in the Journal of Mammalogy shows that Madagascan flying foxes are physically shrinking over time.
